transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
I feel like I’ve lost my drive and personality. I just don't have the energy or motivation to do anything anymore, even the art and routines that used to keep me going.

Did these changes start after a specific stressful event or major life change, or did they come on without a clear trigger? Have you had any similar episodes of depression or loss of interest in the past?

Yes, everything really started going downhill after a painful divorce about two and a half years ago, which forced me to move into a small studio and live on a much tighter budget. I've never had an episode like this before in my life, as I used to be really active with my art, hobbies, and friends.

When you feel at your lowest, have you had thoughts of wanting to die or hurt yourself, or have you ever heard or seen things that other people don’t? This helps me understand how severe the depression is.

I don't have plans to hurt myself, though I constantly feel like a burden who deserves to be punished. I do hear things, though—almost every day a male voice behind my right ear tells me I'm pathetic and a failure, and it won't stop even when I put on headphones.

When you hear this voice, does it only happen during periods when you feel depressed, or has it also happened when your mood was otherwise okay? Has the voice ever told you to harm yourself or anyone else?

Actually, the voice happens even when my mood is relatively okay, like last summer when I didn't feel especially sad, just flat, but I still heard it most days. It has never told me to harm myself or anyone else, though. It just puts me down constantly, calling me pathetic and a failure.

Have there been times when you heard the voice for at least 2 weeks while you were not depressed at all, and during those times did you also have other symptoms like feeling watched, believing things others said were untrue, or your thoughts becoming jumbled?

Yes, last summer there was a stretch of a few weeks where I didn't feel especially sad, just very flat, but the voice still talked to me almost every day. During those same weeks, I was also completely convinced that my neighbors were watching me and reporting on what I was doing. It felt just as real then as it does when my mood is at its lowest.

Outside of times when you hear the voice or feel watched, have you ever had a period lasting at least 2 weeks where you felt clearly depressed most of the day nearly every day? Or have the low mood and loss of interest been present for most of the illness overall?

The heavy, drained feeling has basically been there the entire time since things fell apart after the divorce. Even during those stretches when the voice or the paranoia eased up a bit, the low mood and lack of energy never really went away. It has definitely been present for the vast majority of this whole period.

inference_history.note: Previously the candidates were [F32.2, F32.1, F43.2]. Based on this conversation, the list changes because psychotic symptoms are now clearly present: the patient reports a persistent auditory hallucination occurring almost daily. This makes the prior non-psychotic depressive candidates less likely. F43.2 becomes less likely because the symptoms have persisted for about 2.5 years and include ongoing hallucinations, which are not well explained by a simple stress-related adjustment picture. A severe depressive episode with psychotic symptoms is now a candidate because of marked depressive symptoms plus hallucinations. A recurrent depressive psychotic condition is also considered because the duration is long, though the patient denies prior episodes, so it is less supported. However, because the voice also occurs when mood is relatively okay, a primary psychotic-spectrum condition must be considered, including a schizophrenia-spectrum disorder and a schizoaffective depressive type picture. More questioning is needed about delusions, disorganization, negative symptoms, functional decline, duration of psychosis outside mood episodes, and any past manic symptoms before making a final diagnosis.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has persistent depressive symptoms for most of a 2.5-year illness course along with chronic psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations and persecutory delusions). Critically, psychotic symptoms were present for at least several weeks during a period without a full depressive episode, supporting schizoaffective disorder, depressive type, rather than major depressive disorder with psychotic symptoms.
